purpose: Tamper-evident, signed proof that a fleet node reconstructed an original payload from a k-of-n erasure shard set. Binds the contributing shard commitments, the coding parameters actually used, and the reconstructing node identity under a keyed-authenticity signature, so any party can detect silent corruption or false reconstruction claims (Byzantine-blame assignment) without access to the original data.

coding_scheme.description: The gossip erasure lane is a systematic XOR single-parity code: one parity shard recovers at most one missing data shard. This is NOT Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8); the receipt records the real scheme identifier and (k, n) plan and never fabricates Reed-Solomon polynomial coefficients the implementation does not compute. A wider code would introduce a new scheme id and a new receipt schema version.

determinism: receipt_commitment is a SHA-256 content hash over a length-prefixed canonical preimage. Every variable-length field (schema_id, shard_set_id, coding_scheme, per-shard origin_node, reconstructing_node, extension keys/values) is prefixed with its u64 big-endian byte length before its bytes; fixed-width scalars are big-endian; the ErasureShardRole is a single tag byte (Data=0, Parity=1); the Option<u16> recovery slot carries an explicit tag byte (0 => None, 1 => Some) so None cannot collide with Some(0). Contributing shards are emitted in strictly-increasing shard_index order. Two honest implementations agree byte-for-byte on the commitment, mirroring compute_erasure_shard_hash in the fleet protocol.

receipt_fields.shard_set_id: string; stable identifier shared by all shards of the reconstructed set
receipt_fields.payload_hash: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256); content hash of the reconstructed original payload
receipt_fields.payload_len: u64; byte length of the reconstructed original payload
receipt_fields.contributing_shards: array of shard_commitment; the shards that materially fed reconstruction (present data shards, plus the parity shard iff a data shard was recovered), in strictly-increasing shard_index order
receipt_fields.recovered_shard_index: Option<u16>; the data-shard index recovered from parity, or null when every data shard was directly present
receipt_fields.reconstructing_node: NodeId; identity of the node that performed the reconstruction
receipt_fields.receipt_commitment: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256) over the length-prefixed canonical preimage of all fields above
receipt_fields.signature: MessageSignature { signer: NodeId, hash: AuthenticityHash }; keyed-authenticity (HMAC-SHA256) signature over receipt_commitment, keyed by the reconstructing node's identity. Same signing primitive as every other fleet gossip message.
receipt_fields.extensions: map<string,string>; forward-compatible extension fields, sorted and length-prefixed into the commitment

shard_commitment_fields.shard_index: u16; index of the shard within its set
shard_commitment_fields.shard_hash: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256); the shard's canonical content hash as recorded on the ErasureShard
shard_commitment_fields.origin_node: NodeId; node that originally encoded the shard
shard_commitment_fields.sequence: u64; per-origin sequence number of the shard

verification.verify: ReconstructionReceipt::verify() — validates schema id, coding scheme, structural invariants (well-formed plan; canonical shard ordering; role-vs-index consistency; recovery consistency: a recovered index is a real data slot that is not directly present and requires exactly one missing data shard plus a parity shard), signer == reconstructing_node, recomputed commitment == receipt_commitment (constant-time), and signature authenticates the commitment (constant-time). Requires NEITHER the original payload NOR the shards. This is the path other fleet nodes use to validate a receipt without performing reconstruction themselves.
verification.verify_against_shards: ReconstructionReceipt::verify_against_shards(shards, reconstruct) — first runs verify(), then cross-checks every committed shard hash against the supplied shard set (recomputing each shard's hash and checking role/origin/sequence/set-id/plan/payload_hash agreement). When reconstruct=true it re-runs reconstruct_erasure_payload over the contributing shards and confirms the reproduced payload hashes to payload_hash. This is the stronger check a party runs when it holds the shards but not necessarily the original payload.

audit_ledger.semantics: Append-only, dedup-keyed on receipt_commitment. record() verifies a receipt before admission (a failing receipt is never stored), returns Ok(true) for a newly-recorded receipt and Ok(false) for an idempotent duplicate. summary_hash() is a deterministic digest over all recorded commitments in insertion order (length-prefixed). The dedup index is #[serde(skip)]; call reindex() once after deserialization to restore dedup semantics.

performance: Receipt generation cost is O(contributing_shards) hash mixes plus one SHA-256 over the commitment preimage and one HMAC-SHA256 signature — bounded well under the 5ms per-reconstruction overhead budget for realistic fleet shard counts. Generation adds no reconstruction work beyond the single reconstruct_erasure_payload call the payload already requires.

tests.unit: crates/franken-engine/src/erasure_reconstruction_receipts.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (>=20 cases: generation happy path, parity recovery, canonical ordering, verify without data, verify against shards, tamper detection for commitment/field/signature/signer, unknown schema/scheme, serde round-trip, determinism, ledger record/dedup/reindex/summary, boundary k=1 and k=n, structural rejections, empty payload, extensions binding)
tests.integration: crates/franken-engine/tests/erasure_reconstruction_receipts_integration.rs (>=30 cases: fleet-state reconstruction, cross-node verification without shards, multi-set ledger accumulation, partition recovery, end-to-end tamper detection, serde persistence)
